source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Florence Nightingale's theory focuses on using which factor to help the patient recover?
questions.rationale: Nightingale's Environmental Theory uses the patient's environment (fresh air, pure water, drainage, cleanliness, light) to assist recovery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)
questions.quote: Act of utilizing ENVIRONMENT of the patient to assist him in his recovery

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theorist described 14 fundamental needs the nurse helps the client meet toward independence?
questions.rationale: Henderson's Nature of Nursing Model has the nurse assist people to gain independence in meeting 14 fundamental needs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)
questions.quote: 14 Fundamental Needs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theorist identified 21 nursing problems?
questions.rationale: Abdellah's Patient-Centered Approaches to Nursing identifies 21 nursing problems.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)
questions.quote: Identifies 21 nursing problems

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Imogene King's theory views nursing as an interaction leading to what?
questions.rationale: King's Goal Attainment Theory sees nursing as nurse-patient interaction leading to goal attainment, with personal, interpersonal, and social systems.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Viewed nursing as an interaction process between patient and nurse that lead to goal attainment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theory says caring is universal but its expression varies by culture?
questions.rationale: Leininger's Cultural Care Diversity and Universality theory holds that caring is universal but culturally expressed, with three intervention modes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Emphasizes that human caring, although universal, varies among cultures

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Myra Levine's model proposes conservation of which?
questions.rationale: Levine's four conservation principles: energy, structural integrity, personal integrity, and social integrity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Conservation of energy

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theorist classified stressors as intrapersonal, interpersonal, and extrapersonal?
questions.rationale: Neuman's Health Care Systems Model addresses stressors within, between, and outside the person; nursing maintains system stability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: intrapersonal stressors (within the individual), interpersonal (occurs between individuals ) and extra personal

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client unable to perform any self-care after a stroke needs which Orem nursing system?
questions.rationale: Wholly compensatory care is for those unable to control their environment and process information; partly compensatory for some activities; supportive-educative for learning self-care.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Wholly Compensatory- for individuals who are unable to control and monitor their environment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A new diabetic needs teaching to give his own insulin. Which Orem system applies?
questions.rationale: Supportive-educative care is for clients who need to learn self-care measures with assistance.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Supportive-Educative- for clients who need to learn to perform self-care measure

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What are the phases of Peplau's interpersonal relations model?
questions.rationale: Peplau described orientation, identification, exploitation, and resolution in the therapeutic nurse-client relationship.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Orientation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theorist views the person as an irreducible energy field, greater than the sum of parts?
questions.rationale: Rogers' Science of Unitary Human Beings sees the person as an irreducible, four-dimensional energy field.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)
questions.quote: Views the person as an irreducible whole, the whole being is greater than the sum of its parts

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is one of Roy's four adaptive modes?
questions.rationale: Roy's adaptive modes are physiologic, self-concept, role-function, and interdependence.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)
questions.quote: Role-function mode

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In Lydia Hall's model, which circle involves the therapeutic use of self?
questions.rationale: Care is nurturance exclusive to nursing; core is therapeutic use of self and reflection; cure is nursing related to physician's orders.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)
questions.quote: Core- involves the therapeutic use of self

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Ida Orlando's three elements of the nursing situation are client behavior, nurse reaction, and:
questions.rationale: Orlando's Dynamic Nurse-Patient Relationship: client behavior, nurse reaction, and nurse action.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)
questions.quote: Nurse action

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which theorist made caring the central, unifying focus of nursing with 10 carative factors?
questions.rationale: Watson's Human Caring Theory centers practice on caring, using 10 carative factors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)
questions.quote: Practice of caring is central to nursing: it is the unifying focus for practice

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse with 2–3 years' experience coordinates complex care and plans well. Which Benner stage is this?
questions.rationale: Competent nurses (2–3 years) show organization and planning and coordinate multiple complex care demands.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Coordinates multiple complex care demands

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse acts because 'it felt right,' without needing rules. Which Benner stage?
questions.rationale: Experts perform fluidly without rules or maxims, often acting on intuition.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Inclined to take a certain action because “it felt right”.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A proficient nurse (3–5 years) is characterized by which?
questions.rationale: Proficient nurses perceive situations holistically, use maxims, and focus on long-term goals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Perceives situations as a whole rather than in terms of parts

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nurse role helps clients exercise their rights and speak for themselves?
questions.rationale: The advocate protects the client and helps them exercise their rights.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Roles of a Nurse (PDF p. 5)
questions.quote: Nurse assist clients in exercising their rights and help them speak for themselves

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: In the communication process, the message returned by the receiver is called:
questions.rationale: Feedback is the response returned by the receiver to the sender.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communication (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Response/feedback- message returned by the receiver to the sender

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which record type groups data by problem and includes a database, problem list, plan, and progress notes?
questions.rationale: The POMR has four components: database, problem list, initial plan, and progress notes (SOAPIE).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Documentation (PDF p. 7)
questions.quote: 4 BASIC COMPONENTS OF POMR

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which documentation tool may be written in pencil for frequently changing care details?
questions.rationale: The Kardex is a concise, quickly updated organizer that may be written in pencil.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Kardex (PDF p. 7)
questions.quote: May be written in a pencil to ease in recording frequent change in details of client care

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which entry is the BEST nurses' note?
questions.rationale: Accurate notes record facts and observations, not opinions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Fact “ Client refused Medication”

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should nursing care be documented?
options: At the end of the shift
As soon as possible after care
questions.rationale: No recording is done before care; documenting is done as soon as possible after assessment or intervention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 7)
questions.quote: No recording should be done BEFORE providing nursing care

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a blank space in a nurses' note be handled?
options: Draw a line through it and sign
questions.rationale: Write on every line; if a blank appears, draw a line through it and sign.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: If a blank appears in the notation, draw a through the blank space and sign the notation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client refuses a treatment. What should be documented?
questions.rationale: Care omitted because of refusal is recorded with what, why, and who was notified.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Document what and why it is omitted and who was notified

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which practice is correct when receiving a telephone order?
options: Write it and read it back
questions.rationale: Only RNs receive telephone orders; they write the date, time, and complete order, read it back, and question unusual orders.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Telephone Orders (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Write the complete order and read it back.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the purpose of the change-of-shift report (endorsement)?
questions.rationale: Endorsement gives a quick summary of needs and care for continuity; it is not merely reciting the Kardex.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Reporting (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: For continuity of care of clients by providing quick summary of health care needs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Who may read a client's chart?
questions.rationale: Only health professionals participating in the client's care may read the chart.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Only the health professionals who participate in the care of the client are allowed to read the chart
